sections.howToEatIt: Chop the leaves and tender stems into salsas, curries, rice and salads.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for cilantro (coriander).

cautions.text: Cilantro (coriander) contains vitamin K. If you take warfarin or a similar blood thinner, keep your intake steady and tell your clinician.
cautions.source: NIH ODS Vitamin K (interaction with warfarin and other anticoagulants)

cilantro.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).

dill.name: Dill

sections.whatItOffers: Dill (raw): 1 cup sprigs gives about 4 calories, with vitamin C (about 10%). Percentages are of the NIH reference intake for adult women.
sections.howToEatIt: Use fresh sprigs with fish, potatoes, yoghurt sauces and pickles.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for dill.

tomato-paste.name: Tomato paste

sections.whatItOffers: Tomato paste (canned): 1 tablespoon gives about 13 calories, with potassium (about 6%). Percentages are of the NIH reference intake for adult women.
sections.howToEatIt: Fry a spoonful in oil at the start of a sauce or stew to deepen the flavour.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for tomato paste.
